title: Tool-call typed output lost during streaming: booleans/numbers coerced to strings and parser failures
creator: Marco Reyes
description: Multiple production customers (hosted API, dedicated pools, and private/VPC installs) reported that tool/function-call responses returned by models were arriving as broken or incorrectly typed structured output when delivered over streaming. Symptoms include JSON parse errors, numeric values and booleans being coerced into strings, and intermittent downstream failures in customers' ingestion pipelines. This ticket tracks investigation, hotfix, and rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use tool/function calling with structured schema (example: {"action":"charge", "amount": 25.0, "success": true})
2) Enable streaming responses (hosted: SSE/chunked HTTP; dedicated: gRPC streaming; private: customer-provided LB with chunking)
3) Observe that on some flows the client receives partial chunks ending before the final '}' and the platform parser attempts to coerce/repair the message
4) In affected cases the platform's reparsing path produces values as strings (e.g., "25.0" or "true") or drops fields leading to downstream schema validation errors.
customer_reports: Customer A (payments platform, hosted): intermittent failures in payment processing; root cause traced to 'amount' becoming string '25.0' in their validation layer.
Customer B (adtech, dedicated): batch jobs fail when boolean flags returned by tools are quoted; occurs on high-throughput bursts.
Customer C (healthcare, private): controlled on-prem environment showed same failure when network MTU combined with gateway re-chunking produced early chunk boundaries.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (2026-03-02): reproduced locally by simulating chunk boundary mid-object using both HTTP chunked and gRPC streaming transports.

Root cause hypothesis: streaming boundary handler was performing an eager 'repair' that attempted to close JSON objects by appending '}' when EOF-like chunk observed; a secondary codepath routed through a legacy JSON5-like lenient parser that coerced primitives to strings.
Dedicated-specific observation: gRPC message framing + our PB->JSON intermediary path sometimes reserializes values, losing numeric type metadata for floats in scientific notation.
Private-specific observation: external LBs in customer envs will sometimes split chunks at different offsets; our parser assumed balanced braces within single received chunk which is unsafe.
Logs: streamer_buffer metrics spike correlated with higher incidence; parser_repair_count incremented for affected requests.
Risk: current repair logic can create valid JSON but with different types than intended. This is causing silent data corruption for strict consumers.
mitigation_deployed: 2026-03-04: Hotfix rolled to hosted runtime that disables lenient reparsing and instead buffers up to N chunks or until matching braces are balanced. Feature flag 'streaming.strict_json' introduced and enabled for all hosted traffic. Dedicated pools received a coordinated hotpatch for pools with customer escalations.
resolution_plan: 1) Implement robust streaming JSON combinator that incrementally parses tokens and waits for syntactic completion rather than naive brace-counting (owner: Jin Park).
2) Replace legacy JSON5 fallback with a typed-aware reparsing routine that preserves number/boolean types where possible (owner: Aisha Khan).
3) Add transport-specific test harnesses (HTTP chunked, gRPC framed, and customer-like LB re-chunking) and integrate into CI to prevent regressions.
4) Backfill e2e tests that exercise tool-call schemas with nested objects, arrays, scientific notation numbers, and explicit booleans.
5) Coordinate private customer patches and provide upgrade steps + checksum of runtime artifact.
rollback_plan: If post-deploy datapoints show increased error rate or latency regressions, flip feature flag 'streaming.strict_json' to false and rollback the runtime image for affected pools. Run binary search on recent commits to identify the regression point and revert the minimal change set.
postmortem_follow_up_tasks: Document the streaming parsing contract in the public API guide and add guidance for customers on how to handle partial chunks.
Add observability: expose parser_repair_count and typed_coercion_rate to Console dashboards and alert when >0.1% of requests are repaired.
Schedule a retrospective with support/solutions engineers to review customer communication and SLA remediation credits where appropriate.
Hardening: add fuzz-tests for chunk boundary scenarios into the runtime fuzz harness.
assignee_updates: 2026-03-03 Aisha Khan: shipped initial strict-json feature flag + hosted rollout to 100% for low-traffic regions. Observed decrease in customer errors for two reported customers.
2026-03-06 Marco Reyes: deployed dedicated hotpatch to impacted pools, coordinated with SRE to monitor tail latency. One dedicated customer confirmed fix in staging.
2026-03-09 Aisha Khan: merged typed-reparse-fix and started canary rollout to runtime-1.22; no regressions observed in canary window. Planning full release 2026-03-11.
2026-03-10 Jin Park: added transport re-chunk CI jobs and unit tests for incremental parser.
notes_for_support: When customers report similar issues ask for raw streaming request/response capture (with PII redacted).
Provide workaround: disable streaming (non-streaming API will return complete object) or enable platform-side 'strict_json' flag if available in Dedicated/Private with guidance.
Provide recommended runtime version: runtime-1.22+ with patch IDs listed in linked_prs.
